dedupe_keys.name: traffic light control using deep reinforcement learning

description: The thesis implements decentralized reinforcement-learning controllers with a constrained action space and compares state representations and reward functions. Q-learning, Deep Q-Network and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient variants are assessed for varying demand in three networks extracted from Lisbon: one intersection, an arterial network and a grid. The related methodology paper defines reproducible simulation setup and evaluation steps. These are implemented simulation controllers, not evidence of deployment on the city’s signal hardware. A catalogue link to a later generic data-distribution code project has uncertain component scope and is not claimed as the exact controller release. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with restricted document or data access and licence label not stated. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened.
